rates.applies_to: Hopper GH100 (H100 PCIe/SXM5/NVL, H200 SXM/NVL, H800, H20, GH200)
rates.notes: Non-tensor: Best Practices Guide column 9.0 (f16x2 128 = 256 halves, FP32 128, FP64 64 results; x2). Tensor: NVIDIA Hopper blog 'the H100 SM ... doubles the A100 raw SM computational power on all previous Tensor Core, FP32, and FP64 data types, clock-for-clock' and 'quadruples ... due to the introduction of FP8', applied to the A100 per-SM rates (FP64 tensor 128->256, TF32 1024->2048, FP16/BF16 2048->4096, INT8 4096->8192, FP8 = 4 x A100 FP16 = 8192). The blog lists 'FP8, FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, and INT8 MMA data types' (no INT4), and FP6/FP4 arrive with Blackwell, so those are 0. CLOCK CAVEAT: NVIDIA's published H100 tensor peaks use a lower clock than the boost clock used for FP32/FP64. H100 SXM (H100 page): FP32 67 TF = 132 x 256 x 1980 MHz, but dense FP16 989.5 TF (half of 1,979 sparse) = 132 x 4096 x 1830 MHz (factor 0.924). H100 NVL: FP32 60 TF = 132 x 256 x 1785 MHz (product brief PB-11773 boost 1,785 MHz), but dense FP16 835.5 TF = 132 x 4096 x ~1545 MHz (factor 0.866). Deriving tensor peaks with the boost clock therefore overstates NVIDIA's figures by about 8% (SXM) to 15% (NVL); multiply tensor results by these factors to reproduce NVIDIA's numbers. FP32/FP64/FP64-tensor figures match the boost clock.

rates.applies_to: Blackwell GB100/B200 (B100, HGX/DGX B200, GB200)
rates.notes: Non-tensor: Best Practices Guide column 10.0 (f16x2 64 = 128 halves, FP32 128, FP64 64 results; x2): FP16/BF16 non-tensor equal FP32 on Blackwell (H100 was 2x). Tensor: NVIDIA publishes no per-SM rate or boost clock for B200. Ratios in the Blackwell technical brief HGX B200 per-GPU column (FP32 75 TF; TF32 1.1, FP16/BF16 2.2 (datasheet 2.25), FP8/FP6 4.5, FP4 9, INT8 4.5 dense PF; 'FP64 Tensor Core | FP64 37 TF' combined row) relative to the FP32 rate of 256 give, at the FP32 clock, TF32 ~3755-3840, FP16 ~7680, FP8 ~15360, FP4 ~30720, INT8 ~15360, FP64 tensor ~126 => the power-of-two architectural rates above with a tensor clock 15/16 of the FP32 clock (with 148 SMs: FP32 at ~1980 MHz, tensor at ~1856 MHz). The same 5th-generation rates (FP16 8192, FP8 16384, FP4 32768 dense per SM per clock) are reproduced exactly by Jetson Thor at its single published 1.57 GHz (see CC 11.0). GB200 per-GPU figures (FP32 80, FP16 2.5 PF) imply a tensor/FP32 clock factor of ~0.98. The FP64 tensor rate equals the non-tensor FP64 rate (combined row). INT4 is absent from the Blackwell supported data-type table (FP64, FP32, TF32, FP16, BF16, FP8, INT8, FP6, FP4), so 0.

rates.applies_to: Blackwell Ultra GB110/B300 (HGX/DGX B300, GB300, DGX Station GB300)

Tensor: Blackwell technical brief HGX B300 per-GPU column has the same TF32 (1.1), FP16/BF16 (2.2), FP8/FP6 (4.5 PF) and FP32 (75 TF) as HGX B200, so those per-SM rates are the CC 10.0 ones; FP4 dense 14 PF vs FP16 2.2-2.25 PF (GB300: 15 vs 2.5) is 6 x FP16 => 49152 (Blackwell Ultra blog: 1.5x Blackwell dense NVFP4). 'FP64 Tensor Core | FP64 1.2 TF' (combined row) -> 1.2/75 x 256 = 4.1 => 4. INT8 dense 0.15 POPS vs FP32 75 TF -> 2 x FP32 => 512 ops/clk/SM, derived at the FP32 clock (GB300 NVL72 rack: 12 PF INT8 / 72 GPUs vs 80 TF FP32 -> ~533; DGX Station lists 330 TOPS sparse). Same tensor-clock caveat as CC 10.0. INT4 not in the supported-type table.
